rule_0.statement: THE HIND RIDE: the body rides its hinds; the walk phase's death triad (the trunk fold, the R hind's 1.981 m/s skid, the capture reflex jumping the R hind to phase 0.95 INTO the skid) has ONE root, and the root is THE CAPTURE REFLEX'S ARMING LAW ITSELF. THE DERIVATION (Rule 1 -- every number below measured on the byte-exact baseline before any edit, from a per-tick census in gait_unit.cpp with the controller byte-untouched): at the reflex's fire decision state (tick 65) the machinery's own strict containment test reported the CoM strictly INSIDE the support hull (com_in_hull=1), yet the reflex fired -- because capture_reflex tests the LEXICOGRAPHICALLY SORTED POINT CLOUD that support_state leaves in its out-parameter, not the monotone-chain convex polygon it builds locally: the sorted cloud is a self-intersecting pseudo-polygon, its per-edge 'outside' test is satisfied on edges the true hull does not have (measured: pseudo-edge from (0.182939,+0.019955) holds the CoM +0.004568 m 'outside' with the pelvis velocity dot positive through vx~=+0.6 m/s, while the true chain holds the CoM inside). The reflex then chose as its capture leg the hind whose pair-min gap sat 1.6e-7 m above the band edge (1.016e-5 vs kTouch 1e-5 -- a GRAZING foot straddling the contact band, not a swung leg) with its stance clock at phase 0.0235 (15x below the 0.68 toe-off), and jumped it to 0.95: a 51.5 deg hip step, a 52.4 deg MP step, joint speeds to 5.7-7.0 rad/s within 5 ticks, the foot slammed into a contact that was mid-arrest. THE CAUSAL VERDICT (stated before the fix, from the trace's tick-ordering and the force balances): REFLEX-FIRST. (1) THE SKID: the R hind's loaded skid onset is its landing at ~55 (rxn 9.9 N at slip 0.742 m/s -- the foot arrives moving with the body); through [55,64] the cone ARRESTS it (0.742 -> 0.453 m/s, -0.032 m/s per tick = 9.7 m/s^2 under mu*N = 5.9-7.2 N: demand INSIDE the cone, m_eff ~ 0.61 kg); the skid was survivable and decaying. (2) THE REFLEX: fires at 65 INTO that arrest (and again at 80 into the fully destabilized state -- capture_events=2); within one tick of the fire the slip's rate REVERSES (+0.254 m/s per tick), the reaction spikes 8.5 -> 12.5 -> 18.6 -> 21.5 N, and the slip runs to 1.981-2.0 m/s: the retarget's demand is ~8x the cone (the capped 11.2125 N.m hip at 5.7 rad/s on a ~0.4 m lever ~ 28 N horizontal demand vs mu*N = 11.2 N). (3) THE FOLD: the posture servo rails from <= tick 50 (the wave-10 ramp's target outrunning the lean dynamics through the settle -- benign, the trunk tracking, the entry green); the commanded target IS the vault table (the designed un-lean, -11.83 deg at the capture -> -5.47 at 79); the actual angle TRACKS (lagging) until the fire -- the trunk pitch speed reverses in the fire tick itself (+0.2811 -> -0.0602 rad/s) and the nose-down run-away (-1.02 rad/s by 75) is the R hind's post-slam plow dragging the trunk against the now positively-railed servo. The skid precedes the fire but was ARRESTING; the fold's rail precedes everything but is CONSTANT through settle and walk and does not discriminate the death tick; the fire is the sole event that converts the arrest into the fatal plow and the storm that exhausts gait_impact_event_budget at 80. THE ONE MECHANISM follows the verdict: (a) THE ARMING LAW, three derived clauses -- (i) THE TRUE-HULL CLAUSE: the containment test runs on the monotone-chain convex hull (the doc's own law, 'CoM projection exits the hull'), computed on the chain support_state already builds, never on the sorted cloud; (ii) THE SWING-CLOCK CLAUSE: only a leg whose clock is in its swing window (phi >= TOE_OFF = 0.68, the machinery's own sampled toe-off -- no new constant) may be jumped: a stance-clock leg's contact loss is instability, not swing, and the reflex WAITS for the clock to bring the leg to swing (the re-stabilization the membrane names); (iii) THE SLIP-CONE CLAUSE: no fire while any touching sole's slip exceeds the derived bound v_bound = mu * g * (1-CAPTURE_PHI) * T_CYCLE = 0.6 * 9.80665 * 0.05 * 0.71 = 0.2089 m/s -- the friction cone's arrest capacity (mu*g on a weight-loaded pad) integrated over the capture's own touchdown window (the (1-CAPTURE_PHI)*T_CYCLE = 0.0355 s the jump itself grants before the TD completes): a contact slipping faster than the cone can arrest inside that window cannot be stabilized by the retarget -- the measured wave-19/20 fingerprint. All constants are the machinery's own (mu from the store, g from the constructor, CAPTURE_PHI, T_CYCLE, TOE_OFF class constants); no number was tuned. THE REJECTED TWO, with the measured reason: (b) skid-first (the hind force/schedule law at the landing phase) -- the pre-fire balance shows the tier law's demand INSIDE the cone at every tick of [55,64] (the schedule was frozen at the settle's 0.5 column, the targets held, the slip decaying at a measured 9.7 m/s^2): there is no lawful correction to make; a hind-side law would tune against a transient that only the fire reversed. (c) fold-first (the walk-phase posture blend re-derived) -- the commanded target is the vault table by construction (compare: the status target_deg equals theta*(phi) at every measured tick), the trunk tracked it until the fire, and the run-away's onset tick IS the fire tick: re-deriving the blend tunes away a symptom whose cause the verdict already names.
